newsitem.title: GERMANY: German equities again follow Wall Street lower.
newsitem.headline: German equities again follow Wall Street lower.

text.p: German equities fell in late afternoon trade, yet again following Wall Street as the Dow Jones index plunged nearly one percentage point in early trade.
At 1418 GMT the IBIS DAX was down 16.63 points at 2,532.21, having recovered lost ground earlier in the afternoon, though still off session lows.
The Dow Jones index was down 41.43 points, or 0.73 percent, at 5606.22 at the same time, also off earlier lows.
The dollar was also weaker, having gained over half a pfennig after comments by Buba President Hans Tietmeyer that U.S. fundamentals should allow the dollar to be stronger.

Traders said that market players were winding up positions in advance of the long weekend in the U.S., as Monday's Labor Day holiday means the U.S. markets will be closed and volumes in Frankfurt are expected to be low.

"Even though we took a hit after last night's close on Wall Street, I still think the German share market is proving remarkably resilient to U.S. data -- we haven't seen a serious correction yet," said a Frankfurt trader.
"Volumes go down as the index goes down, and volumes go up as the market goes up, which is the sign of a healthy market," the trader added.
Dealers said that next week the market would look around for direction, but that there was little data there likely to move the market.

Dealers said the market would seek inspiration from August German jobless data on Thursday, and U.S. payroll data on Friday, dealers said, but trade could be mixed until then with little corporate news to move the market.
Shares in the news on Friday included AGIV AG, which fell nearly seven percent to 24.50 marks despite reporting a 4.8 percent increase in six-month sales and a gain in orders in hand.
Daimler Benz was lower in late trade, down 55 pfennigs at 80.30 marks, but off earlier lows. Dealers said the share fell as any expectation about future gains had been taken out of the share.
